Earlier this year, when Apple launched the MacBook Neo, the personal computer market was clearly caught off guard. Although the aggressive pricing strategy of the laptop has since been adjusted to market conditions, Windows阵营 rivals have taken several months to gradually unveil their counterattack products. HP is joining the fray today, launching a new laptop equipped with an OLED screen, also starting at $699 — though with quite a few strings attached.

Overall, the HP OmniBook 5 14 looks much like a MacBook Neo chassis in a colourful budget version, paired with the more refined, understated greens and blues of the Apple iPad Air series. Underneath the 14-inch screen, the body is just 11.77mm thick and weighs only 2.56 pounds — perfectly timed for the back-to-school shopping season, yet HP somehow missed that window. The real highlight of this machine is that 14-inch display — at this price point, you'd normally only see an IPS panel, but this time you have two OLED options to choose from, with details to follow. On either side of the body are two full-function USB-C ports and a headphone jack; opening the lid reveals an FHD camera, and Windows Hello is supported.

Regarding hardware specifications, HP says the laptop supports up to an Intel Core 7 processor, but the model on display only showed a single configuration. The battery life on the spec sheet is rather impressive — up to 42 hours of local video playback (battery capacity not specified) — though admittedly, local video playback tests may not fully reflect real-world usage. HP mentions the machine is compatible with its 65W GaN mini-charger, which is expected to be included in the box. Beyond that, the known specs also include dual microphones and audio tuned by Poly Studio; if you feel there's still a lot of information missing, you're definitely not alone.

First, the processor model of the $700 version of this laptop remains unknown, making it hard to directly compare with Apple's A18 Pro. HP has also chosen not to disclose any information on storage or memory configurations — not even an 'up to' figure — which precisely reflects the enormous pressure the PC market is under amid the current memory supply crunch. Even the most eye-catching selling point comes with a fatal trade-off: HP spent quite a bit of time at the launch event describing that 2.5K OLED display, but that version won't ship until March 2027. The model going on sale later this month at Best Buy comes with a 2K OLED display, but brightness drops dramatically from 650 nits to just 300 nits.

Given all these unspecified details, and some answers that are disappointing, if HP has still managed to pique your interest, please keep an eye out for more information to be released before the product officially goes on sale.
